title: The Deception of Baal Prophets and the Drought of Elijah
english: A shadow. Therefore, this one alone gives good things to those asking him, as he is the one whom the soul finds, and as he is the one raising up desire, the Lord, who fills your desire with good things. Faith and knowledge must stand over his giving of the good, so as not to fall into error. For example, thought is a good thing, and a useful good thing is addressed as beautiful.

To say it hymnologically: 'Make good,' learn from the loud-voiced Isaiah to make the beautiful; the Apostle says to hold fast to the beautiful with an apostolic voice: 'Test all things, hold fast to the beautiful, abstain from every kind of evil' (1 Thess 5:21). 'For if anything is good, it is of him; and if anything is beautiful, it is from him,' in harmony with 'milk for young men and fragrant wine for virgins' (1 Cor 3:2), and these things are perceived by the sense of fire and the hand. For it is not spiritual and of a soulful man to not receive the things of the Spirit, regarding such things as folly, so that the senses of the inner man are defiled. For how would the sense of smell and taste not be harmed by not tasting the Lord, according to what was said: 'Taste and see that the Lord is good' (Ps 34:8), and the comprehension of the holy breath of his name, according to: 'Myrrh has been poured out for you, therefore the maidens loved you' (Song 1:3)?

Zach. X, 1–3: You ask for rain from the Lord at the right and wrong time; the Lord made visions and winter rain, he will give to each of them vegetation in the field. Because those who utter maxims spoke labors, and the diviners [spoke] false visions...

They spoke false dreams and made vain calls; therefore they were dried up like sheep and were harmed, because there was no healing. My anger was provoked against the shepherds, and I will visit the lambs.

When wickedness prevails, drought occurs often, as God judges; therefore the one raging against such things is to be calmed, lest falling [into error], as if instead of God they were flattering demons; [it is better] to be calmed, as to receive prophecies and dreams from them. Such a deception occurred to the Hebrews in the times of Elijah the great prophet, when rain did not become upon the earth for three years and six months, as all things were driven to despair, as an assurance of death, and other animals were ruined through the scarcity of their fodder.

This harm having prevailed, it was the custom for Israel, having been benefited many times by God in such things, to be surrounded by Him and to ask rain from Him so that prosperity might exist. This they have not done, because deception has prevailed, as those seeking from idols are able to drink [in] what they are not able to provide. And madness came from Jezebel, the wife of the one ruling the Hebrews, being exceedingly an idolater, as she had ensnared him and her husband.

In her days, therefore, the prophets of Baal increased, being an image of the Sidonians, prophesying and uttering [words] and this very thing being found by them being highlighted in dreams, always daring to follow predictive paths, variously lying when favorable weather arrived, so as to no longer ask for the provision of rain, 'that rises the sun upon the good and the bad and rains upon the just and the unjust' (1 Kings 17:14). Since, therefore, those submitted to [me] have fallen into such ignorance, God, taking pity on those thus submitted, cast upon the prophet to say: 'Ask for rain' (1 Kings 18:41).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
